\section{Exact four-channel retained-state certificate}

Let the regular state be \(0\), and let states \(1,\ldots,k\) denote charged
defect channels.  For \(0<q<1\), define
\begin{equation}
 Q_{0a}=\frac{q^2}{k},\qquad
 Q_{a0}=1,qquad
 Q_{00}=Q_{ab}=0\quad(a,b\ge1).
\end{equation}
The scalar row ceiling is one because return from a charged state is forced.

\begin{proposition}[Exact star eigenweight]
For
\begin{equation}
 V_0=1,
 \qquad
 V_a=q^{-1}\quad(1\le a\le k),
\end{equation}
one has
\begin{equation}
 QV=qV.
\end{equation}
Hence \(\rhoPF(Q)=q\), and the declared weight is the optimal positive
weight.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The regular row is
\[
 (QV)_0=\sum_{a=1}^k\frac{q^2}{k}\frac1q=q=qV_0.
\]
Every charged row is
\((QV)_a=V_0=1=qV_a\).  Positivity and
Theorem~\ref{thm:cw} gives optimality.
\end{proof}

For the package calibration,
\begin{equation}
 q=0.002430277501841998,
 \qquad k=4,
\end{equation}
with channels center, continuous, cut/orbit, and integer topology.  The
charged-state weights are
\begin{equation}
 q^{-1}=411.4756439304\ldots.
\end{equation}
The entry mass per channel is
\(q^2/4=1.4765621839898456\times10^{-6}\).  The exact weighted ceiling is
\(q\), while the scalar ceiling is one.  The numerical eigen-residual in the
reproducibility certificate is below \(9\times10^{-19}\).

This upgrades the earlier finite calibration: the chosen weight was not only
feasible but Perron-optimal for its declared multichannel star kernel.
